memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Let Reuben live and not die, nor his people be few. And this he said about Judah: 'Hear, Lord, the cry of Judah; bring him to his people. With his own hands he defends his cause. Oh, be his help against his foes!'" — Deut 33:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses now begins blessing the individual tribes, starting with Reuben and Judah. For Reuben, the firstborn who had stumbled, the blessing is simple but gracious: "Let Reuben live and not die." Even the tribe with a troubled history is included in the blessing — mercy is extended, not withheld. And for Judah, Moses prays that God would hear his cry, bring him to his people, and be his help against his foes.

There is grace in how Moses blesses even Reuben. This was the tribe descended from the son who had failed his father, yet Moses does not write him off. He blesses him, prays for his survival and flourishing. This is how God deals with His people — not according to our failures, but according to His mercy. Even those with a stained past are included in His blessing.

And in the blessing of Judah, we catch a whisper of something greater. Judah is prayed for as the one who defends and is helped by God — and it was from Judah that the kings of Israel would come, and ultimately the King of kings. The cry "Hear, Lord, the cry of Judah" points forward to the tribe from which the Messiah would be born.

For Jesus is "the Lion of the tribe of Judah" (Rev 5:5). This ancient blessing, prayed over a single tribe, opened onto the coming of the Saviour of the world. So take heart: the God who included even failing Reuben in His mercy is the God who, through the line of Judah, brought forth Christ to save us all. His grace reaches the failing, and His plan brings forth the King.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God's blessing reaches even those with a failed past?
2. How does seeing Christ in the line of Judah deepen my wonder at God's plan?
3. Where do I need to cry out to God as Judah did, for help against my foes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your mercy includes even those who have failed, and that from Judah You brought forth Christ, the Lion and King. Hear my cry, be my help, and thank You for the Saviour born of Your plan. Amen.
